The *Nāga Sutta* (Ud 4.5; PTS Ud 41) is a discourse found in the *Udāna* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text depicts the Buddha, who, feeling hemmed in and crowded by his followers, withdraws into seclusion [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations cataloged on SuttaCentral include 16 versions across 13 languages, including an English rendering by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Additional large Pali-internal shared segments appear in the *Navakanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 9, §1.3–1.8), the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), other Vinaya sections (Kd 1, Kd 6, Kd 8), and multiple nikāya discourses (SN 6, SN 22, SN 35, SN 48, AN 5, AN 6, AN 8), as well as the commentary *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
